claims.text: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts use Pt nanoparticles dispersed on oxide supports such as alumina or undoped ceria.
Pt nanoparticles can be encapsulated within a porous CeO2 shell using controlled deposition and thermal processing.
The proposed processing will produce a uniform porous CeO2 shell surrounding the Pt nanoparticles.
The porous CeO2 shell mediates oxygen storage and release.
The CeO2 shell physically restricts Pt nanoparticle migration.
The CeO2 layer supplies labile oxygen species to Pt sites.
Labile oxygen supplied by the CeO2 layer enhances oxidation reactions at Pt sites.
The CeO2 shell acts as a physical barrier to Pt sintering.
Suppressing Pt sintering sustains catalytic activity and durability.
Encapsulation within a porous CeO2 shell will permit reduced platinum-group-metal loading while maintaining or improving performance.
Relative to conventional Pt catalysts on undoped oxide supports, the encapsulated catalyst will exhibit improved exhaust-pollutant conversion.
Relative to conventional catalysts, the encapsulated catalyst will show less Pt nanoparticle growth after aging.
The predicted benefits will hold under automotive exhaust environments at 300–800°C with alternating oxidizing and reducing conditions.
The benefits depend on the CeO2 shell being uniformly and optimally formed.
Synthesis deviations or extreme operating conditions may diminish the benefits of encapsulation.
